The evidence suggests that Bleomycin may be repurposed for Plasmablastic Lymphoma, a rare and aggressive subtype of lymphoma characterized by dysplastic cells and high proliferation rates. The indirect pathway through Dexamethasone and Carmustine, both chemotherapy agents, indicates a possible role of Bleomycin in the treatment of this disease, though the direct link remains speculative. The scores from the paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in the relationship, but the evidence is not yet robust enough to confirm a direct therapeutic effect. The mechanism of action is not fully elucidated, and further studies are needed to establish the precise role of Bleomycin in the pathogenesis of Plasmablastic Lymphoma.
